references.text: This text also concerns foreigners who wish to celebrate Passover with Israel and states that there shall be one law for both the native and the foreigner.
Here, the foreigner living among the Israelites who wishes to bring a burnt offering or a peace offering to the Lord is mentioned.
The command to treat the foreigner as a native and to love them as yourself.
Refers to foreigners in Israel who wish to present a burnt offering to the Lord.
States that there shall be one regulation for both the foreigner and the native regarding the celebration of Passover.
The continuation of the text elaborating on the principle of one law for both the congregation and the foreigner.
Reiterates the principle that there shall be one law for the native and the foreigner who sins unintentionally.
Paul writes that Gentiles are no longer foreigners and strangers, but fellow citizens with the saints – the fulfillment of the inclusion of foreigners in God's people.
